instruction: Someone stole my card details and made an online purchase. I told my bank 2 working days after getting the SMS. How much do I have to pay?
response: Nothing. Under RBI's July 2017 rules, if the fraud was a third-party breach (neither you nor the bank was at fault) and you report it within 3 working days of the bank's communication, your liability is zero.

instruction: What is my maximum liability if I report a third-party fraud on my regular savings account after 5 working days?
response: Your liability is the transaction value or ₹10,000, whichever is lower, because it was reported within 4 to 7 working days and the account is an ordinary savings account.

instruction: What is the maximum liability for a BSBD account holder who reports a third-party fraud within 4 to 7 working days?
response: ₹5,000, or the transaction value if that is lower.

instruction: I shared my OTP with a caller pretending to be from the bank and lost money. Who bears the loss?
response: Sharing an OTP counts as customer negligence, so you bear the full loss until you report the unauthorised transaction to the bank. Any loss after you report it is borne by the bank. The bank may still choose to waive your liability.

instruction: Within how many days must a bank credit the disputed amount after I report an unauthorised electronic transaction?
response: Within 10 working days of your notification, as a shadow reversal value-dated to the date of the unauthorised transaction, without waiting for any insurance claim.

instruction: Who has to prove that a customer is liable in an unauthorised electronic transaction?
response: The bank. The burden of proving customer liability lies on the bank.

instruction: Money was debited at an ATM but no cash came out. When should I get it back and what if the bank is late?
response: The bank must auto-reverse it within T + 5 days (T is the transaction day). For every day of delay beyond that, the bank must pay you ₹100 automatically, without you needing to complain.

instruction: My UPI transfer to a friend was debited but never credited. What is the turnaround time?
response: The beneficiary bank must reverse the amount by T + 1 day if it cannot credit it, and pay ₹100 per day for any delay beyond T + 1.

instruction: Do I need to file a complaint to get compensation for a failed transaction?
response: No. RBI requires the compensation to be credited automatically once the turnaround time is crossed. If it is not, you can complain under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme.

instruction: Can I complain directly to the RBI Ombudsman without contacting my bank?
response: No. You must first make a written complaint to your bank. You can go to the Ombudsman if the bank does not reply within 30 days, or rejects the complaint, or you are not satisfied with its reply.

instruction: How do I file a complaint with the RBI Ombudsman?
response: Online at https://cms.rbi.org.in, by email to crpc@rbi.org.in, or by post to the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre, Reserve Bank of India, 4th Floor, Sector 17, Chandigarh – 160017. You can also call the toll-free number 14448 for help.

instruction: My bank never replied to my complaint. How long do I have to approach the Ombudsman?
response: Within one year and 30 days from the date you made the complaint to the bank.

instruction: How much compensation can the RBI Ombudsman award?
response: There is no limit on the disputed amount. In addition, the Ombudsman can award up to ₹20 lakh for consequential loss and up to ₹1 lakh for loss of time, expenses, harassment or mental anguish.

instruction: I'm unhappy with the Ombudsman's decision. Can I appeal?
response: Yes. You can appeal to the Appellate Authority (the Executive Director in charge of the RBI department administering the scheme) within 30 days of receiving the award or rejection. A further 30 days may be allowed for sufficient cause.

instruction: Will the Ombudsman take up a complaint about my bank's decision to reject my loan application?
response: Generally no. Complaints about a bank's commercial judgment or commercial decision are not maintainable under the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme.

instruction: How often must a low-risk customer update KYC?
response: At least once every 10 years. Medium-risk customers update every 8 years and high-risk customers every 2 years.

instruction: Nothing in my KYC details has changed. Do I need to visit the branch for re-KYC?
response: No. A self-declaration that nothing has changed is enough, and you can submit it through your registered email or mobile, an ATM, internet or mobile banking, or a letter.

instruction: Is there a minimum balance in a BSBD account and how many free withdrawals do I get?
response: There is no minimum balance. You get at least four free withdrawals a month, and digital payments such as UPI, NEFT, RTGS, IMPS and PoS transactions do not count towards that limit.

instruction: Can I have BSBD accounts in two different banks?
response: No. A customer can hold only one BSBD account across all banks, and the bank takes a declaration that you have no other BSBD account before opening one.

instruction: What are the five rights in RBI's Charter of Customer Rights?
response: Right to Fair Treatment; Right to Transparency, Fair and Honest Dealing; Right to Suitability; Right to Privacy; and Right to Grievance Redress and Compensation.
